findings.title: Test function name not renamed to match the middleware
findings.body: The test function is still named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` even though the file and the middleware it tests were renamed to `MetricsMiddleware`. The diff only updates the internal call to `newMetricsMiddleware`, leaving the outer test name stale, which makes the test hard to find, breaks grep-based filtering (`-run TestMetricsMiddleware`), and signals that the rename was applied incompletely.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
findings.body: The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (and its `instrumentContext` helper, which builds the `endpoint`/`pluginId`/`dsName`/`dsUID`/`uname` attribute slice) is added with 69 lines of behavior but no accompanying `_test.go` file. The previous `instrumentContext` lived inside `instrumentation_middleware.go` and was likewise uncovered, but the move to a dedicated middleware is the right moment to add at least a basic test that verifies the contextual attributes are correctly populated (including the nil checks for `DataSourceInstanceSettings` and `User`) and are present on the downstream context.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses contextual fields if ContextualLoggerMiddleware is removed from the chain
findings.body: The previous `logRequest` explicitly added `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, and `traceID` as explicit log parameters. The new implementation strips all of those from `logParams` and relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` to pick them up from the request context. That only works if `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (which calls `log.WithContextualAttributes`) sits between `MetricsMiddleware` and `LoggerMiddleware` in the chain. Today this is true (see `pluginsintegration.go` lines 158-161), but the dependency is now implicit: any future refactor that reorders, conditionally registers, or removes the contextual-logger middleware will cause `Plugin Request Completed` log lines to silently lose identifying fields (plugin id, datasource uid, user, endpoint, trace id) with no compile-time or test-time signal. Either keep an explicit fallback that logs those fields if they are missing from context, or add a test that asserts the chain ordering.

findings.title: FromContext falls back to a context-less logger when the type assertion fails
findings.body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` does `d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)`. If the type assertion ever fails (e.g. a future change in `pkg/infra/log` returns a different concrete type, or a test fakes the infra logger), the code falls back to `d.New()`, silently discarding every contextual attribute that `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` placed on the context. Since `LoggerMiddleware` now depends on this method to surface `pluginId`/`endpoint`/`uname` in production logs, a silent attribute drop here directly degrades log quality. Returning the asserted value (or logging/returning an error) is safer than constructing a fresh logger with no context.
